evidence: SQLAlchemy _parse_url regex (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/url.py:898-945): after 'sqlite://', host/port groups need a non-slash char, so the '/(?P<database>[^\?]*)' group captures everything after the third slash. sqlite:////tmp/x.db -> '/tmp/x.db'; sqlite:///rel.db -> 'rel.db'; sqlite:///C:/x.db -> 'C:/x.db' (ipv4host excludes '/', port needs ':' directly after '//', which is '/'). Database is only unquoted, no other post-processing. Matches usage at sql_runner.py:52-62.

sqlalchemy url.py _parse_rfc1738_args does int(components['port']) (line ~948), so 'sqlite://:memory:' (port 'memory:') raises ValueError, not ArgumentError; ArgumentError only comes from a regex non-match (e.g. 'nonsense'). ArgumentError is a SQLAlchemyError, not a ValueError. _readonly_uri (sql_runner.py:65-82) emits file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro for drive paths and file:// + '//tmp/x.db' = file:////tmp/x.db?mode=ro for // paths. SQLite's URI parser (sqlite3ParseUri) skips 'file://' and treats the authority as the text up to the next '/'; an empty authority is accepted (only non-empty, non-'localhost' authorities yield 'invalid uri authority'). Both forms have an empty authority, and the SQLite URI docs list file:///... as valid. Based on documented/known SQLite C behavior; the C source is not in the repo and nothing was run.

sql_runner.py:31 defines _WINDOWS_DRIVE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]"), which requires a slash or backslash after the colon. It does NOT match 'C:' without a slash (e.g. 'C:foo.db'), so the second half of the claim is false. The first half holds: 'a:b.db' does not match the regex and goes through the generic branch (lines 79-82). quote(..., safe='/') percent-encodes ':' to %3A, giving file:a%3Ab.db?mode=ro, which SQLite decodes. A drive-relative name like 'C:foo.db' takes the same non-drive path.

sql_runner.py:65-82 _readonly_uri: Windows drive paths (regex ^[A-Za-z]:[\\/], line 31) become file:///C:...; paths starting '//' (UNC-like, '///x.db') get file:// + path, i.e. an explicit empty authority (file:////host/share, file://///x.db); all other paths become file:<quoted path> with no '//' authority at all; backslash UNC '\\host' is percent-encoded (quote) into the path. quote() encodes ':' and '?' '#', so no input can introduce a host part.

sql_runner.py:31 defines _WINDOWS_DRIVE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]') with no os.name/sys.platform check; _readonly_uri (lines 76-78) applies it unconditionally, so 'C:/x.db' yields 'file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro'. On POSIX that URI path is /C:/x.db, not the relative file 'C:/x.db'.

Mechanics confirmed in src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sqlite/sql_runner.py: _WINDOWS_DRIVE = r'^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]' (line 31) matches 'C:\x.db' (accepts backslash); _readonly_uri (lines 76-78) does database_path[:2] + quote(database_path[2:], safe='/'), so the backslash becomes %5C and the URI is file:///C:%5Cx.db?mode=ro. The consequence ('SQLite on Windows may not treat it as a separator') is a hedged claim about Windows SQLite runtime behavior that cannot be settled from the repo source. SQLite percent-decodes URI paths before use, so the filename should decode back to 'C:\x.db', which Windows accepts, but I could not verify this on Windows, and I ran no tests. Command not run: any Windows SQLite connection or the test suite.
